text: For many people, clothes are a way of showing who they are without saying a word. Following trends can also make them feel part of a group, which matters a lot to teenagers. Social media speeds everything up, because influencers show new styles every day. Personally, I only pay attention to trends when I actually need something new, otherwise it gets expensive very quickly.

tips.en: Without saying a word presents clothes as a kind of language.

questions.question: Why do some people follow fashion trends closely?

text: The biggest problem is waste. Cheap clothes are designed to be worn a few times and thrown away, and huge amounts end up in landfill. There are also serious concerns about working conditions in the factories that make them. I think brands should be responsible for recycling their products, but customers play a part too — buying fewer, better things is probably the simplest solution.

tips.en: The biggest problem is waste gives the core of the answer straight away.
tips.kk: The biggest problem is waste — жауаптың өзегі бірден.
tips.ru: The biggest problem is waste — сразу ядро ответа.

text: I don't think they need to wear them every day, but it's nice to see them at celebrations. In Kazakhstan, many young people now wear modern versions of traditional clothing, for example a jacket with national patterns, which is a clever way of keeping the culture alive. It feels more natural than wearing a full costume that only comes out for photos.

text: It depends on the job. For people who meet clients, like bank staff or lawyers, a dress code creates trust and looks professional. But in creative or technical jobs, strict rules often feel unnecessary and can make people less comfortable. Many companies now choose a middle way — no jeans for meetings, but relaxed clothes the rest of the time, which seems sensible to me.

questions.question: Is it a good idea for companies to have a dress code?

text: Partly for economic reasons — you can find good-quality clothes for a fraction of the price. But there's also a change in attitude. A few years ago second-hand shopping had a slightly negative image, whereas now it's seen as smart and environmentally friendly. Apps for selling used clothes have made it much easier too, so young people treat their wardrobe almost like something they can trade.
